episodeSelection.date: c.610 CE; revelation belongs to attributed tradition

historicalSelection.passage: Jonathan E. Brockopp (ed.), The Cambridge Companion to Muhammad, Introduction, excerpt p. 4 / PDF lines 128–149: the account places meditation outside Mecca in 610 and frames the revelation and Gabriel as the Muslim narrative; it dates the Meccan period 610–622.
historicalSelection.qualification: The date and setting are reported through later religious biography. Phrase as 'tradition dates/recounts'; do not narrate revelation, divine speech, or supernatural claims as independently verified fact.
historicalSelection.candidateEvent: Islamic biographical tradition places Muhammad's first revelatory experience around this year. Historical reporting can document that this is the tradition, not establish an angelic visitation or revelation as an objective event.

title.en: Voices among the Market Stalls
title.es-ES: Voces entre los puestos del mercado

historicalSelection.passage: Gerald R. Hawting, The Formation of Islam, chapter “The Origins of the Muslim Community,” lines 279–282: explicitly situates the early prophetic career in the Muslim narrative and the origins of the community in Arabia. Compare Brockopp, Introduction, pp. 4–5, which notes uncertainty over who first joined Muhammad's intimate circle (PDF lines 471–480).
